take_homes: Choose a quality check by running candidates on my own output and scoring them. Reputation and 'are you sure?' don't count.
The judge is a saved file that states what it catches and where it stops. I can show that to my CFO and rerun it.
Small error rates compound across a long chain. A test-and-fix loop is what brings them down.

monday.move: Run the four detectors on last week's pilot-cohort brief, using the Q2 review and the churn article as the evidence roster. Save the winner as a judge file in a place my team can reach.
monday.who: Me first, then one person from my team of fourteen to try the judge file.
monday.when: Monday morning, before the pricing working group send-out.
monday.stop_condition: The judge flags at least one claim I hadn't seen, or I decide it finds nothing the brief didn't already have.
monday.blocker: We have no shared place for context files, so the judge file and the evidence roster would sit on my machine only. A teammate couldn't pick them up.

misconception.why: Picking a winner from a scoreboard is a different kind of work from polishing a prompt. I still think prompts matter, but they're no longer the main thing.

one_line: Skip the legal case slides. The hour you spend running four checks on your own brief and keeping a judge file is the part that's worth it.
